feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The baseline (iteration 0, 60 development trials) went off track on all three tracks with one line-loss event each, progress of 0.04 to 0.12, and max_error of about 0.061 m, just past the 0.06 m limit. rms_error was low (about 0.03 m), so the failure is a transient after the line is lost, not steady drift. This candidate targets that failure directly: sensors spread to x = -0.03 to +0.03 with 16 mm footprints so the outer sensors see the tape sooner, kp cut from 2.0 to 1.5 to soften the turn response, and kd raised from 0.05 to 0.1 to damp it. Two points to check when telemetry arrives. First, the 16 mm footprints overlap heavily with 0.015 m sensor spacing, so the signal resolution is coarser than the baseline's. Watch whether rms_error rises. Second, base_speed was cut from 1.6 to 1.4. At that speed the course may not be covered in 3.0 s, so a clean run that stops short of progress 0.995 would show that speed, not line tracking, is now the limit. Next-race guidance: if line_loss_events is 0 or 1 and max_error stays below 0.06 m but completion is 0 with progress near 1, raise base_speed to 1.6 to 1.7 and keep kp at 1.5. If line_loss_events is still 1 or more with max_error above 0.06 m on the s-bend, reduce base_speed further or raise kd to about 0.15. If the run completes with completion_time well under 2.8 s, the gains are good; keep them and tune speed up.
requested_changes: If the next race shows completion 0 with progress near 1 and no line-loss events, raise base_speed from 1.4 to 1.6-1.7 (the baseline at 1.6 lost the line early, so the speed was not the cause of the baseline failure) while keeping kp 1.5 and kd 0.1.

If line_loss_events is still 1 or more and max_error exceeds 0.06 m on the s-bend, reduce base_speed to about 1.2-1.3 or raise kd to about 0.15 to damp the transient that pushed the baseline off track.
If rms_error rises above about 0.04 m with the 16 mm footprints, reduce sensor_size to 0.012 and keep the wider spread x = -0.03 to +0.03, because the coarser signal may be causing the extra error.
